Anthropic's Economic Scenario publication was a pretty interesting read:

1. Anthropic's "extreme" scenario has GDP growth reaching 15.4% in 2030

So around 7.3x current rates (~2.1% Y/Y), which is consistent with what Elon Musk is saying about outgrowing the national debt with AI.  

2. Almost all of the divergence happens after 2027. 

Their model shows relatively little separation in 2026-2027, then the curves bend sharply into 2028-2030. 

So my read is that it points to 2026-2027 as buildout years and 2028-2030 as economic acceleration. 

Kinda gets mapped as well when you look at $AMZN / $META / $GOOGL capex, and short term FCF headwinds (but massive projected profitability post 2028)

3. In an extreme scenario, unemployment of knowledge workers goes to 17.9%. With 11.9% economy-wide unemployment

"At the individual level, it means coders and call service center agents may have to switch to jobs like electrician and nurse, which are less exposed to AI."

GG computer science majors. 

4. Non-cognitive wages: +33.6% vs. baseline in an extreme scenario. 

So your electricians/construction-type labor becomes extremely valuable? (but this isn't factoring in humanoids yet...)

Whereas -11.5% for knowledge workers in 2030 vs. baseline. 

5. Aggregate capital income is ~81% higher than it would have been without AI

Productivity explodes -> aggregate labor income barely changes -> essentially all of the incremental GDP accrues to capital.

So that makes ownership of capital rather than labor... so equities like compute, power, semis, networking, robotics, etc. become pretty important... 

TLDR:

- Economic growth go brr
- Jobs that require thinking = unemployment + lower wages
- Physical labor = more important, like electricians. 
- AI equities go brrr.

Got an email from the US Department of Justice yesterday: a founder we invested in many years ago has been arrested and is getting charged for Securities Fraud.

He promised the world, raised 8 figures, and eventually delivered the most effortless excuse for a platform, essentially just a frontend, plus a worthless token with no liquidity.

He thought he was being clever by technically delivering his promises on paper, even though it was painfully obvious it was a rug. Something that was basically confirmed by team members who left very soon after the raise over how he operated the company and how he spent the money.

We only invested a small amount, and from experience it didn't feel worth going after. Nothing ever seems to come out of legal cases like this, so we chalked it up to poor founder diligence on our end and moved on.

But we all know how many founders over the last few years were simply extracting from the industry, convinced they could game the system with worthless tokens to fund their lambo-yacht-jetset lifestyle. And for a long time, this has been one of the main problems of crypto, and also the reason why we are getting so much negative press in the real world.

If that was you, or you were planning on it, then yeah, you should be sweating. The days of founders getting away with this are over, and that is massively positive for the industry. Go scam somewhere else.

🚨 $CIFR gets conditional Batch Zero classifications on 3.2 GW of Texas load, likely spread across both "Base" and "Studied".

The Street had been looking for roughly 2 GW of Base Load across Colchis, Mikeska and McLennan, with Apollo (900 MW) and the Stingray expansion (200 MW) submitted as Studied Load.

Obviously the big question is how much of this 3.2 GW is Base vs Studied (the latter containing risk of a haircut unless Cipher can supplement with on-site generation).

Cipher says it is still working with its transmission service providers (TSPs) on the site-level designations before giving more detail next week. This is exactly why they hired Bill Blevins, who joined Cipher in June after serving as ERCOT’s Director of Grid Coordination. Hopefully he’s earning his comp this week.

Recall that just last week Cipher announced it has begun developing gas laterals (small pipelines) capable of supporting up to 2.5 GW of on-site generation. Management had previously said it wouldn’t pursue behind-the-meter generation without "demonstrated" tenant demand.

Lastly don’t forget the 477 MW that doesn’t need to wait for Batch Zero: Odessa (207 MW), Reveille (70 MW) and Ulysses (200 MW) are already through the relevant grid milestones and available to lease today. 

3.2 GW is an encouraging first print that helps validate just how real $CIFR’s enormous development pipeline is. Next week we find out how much is Base Load, and whether the push into on-site generation tells us something about the rest.

Ideally, we also get some detail on how those gas laterals will be financed and whether tenants might fund or reimburse any of the cost.

𝟯. 𝗩𝗼𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝘄𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝘂𝗽. The $VIX is still relatively low, but $VVIX is rising. When the volatility of the $VIX begins moving before the $VIX itself, it can be an early warning that larger investors are starting to pay for protection.

𝟱. 𝗢𝗶𝗹. Oil is approaching $100 again, with no solution in sight. If oil remains this high or moves above $100, it could revive inflation, reduce the possibility of rate cuts and put additional pressure on consumers and corporate margins.

None of these factors guarantees a correction, and I still do not see the final catalyst. But the ingredients are now in place.

I am not turning aggressively bearish. I am simply reducing some risk and adding hedges while protection is still relatively cheap.
